answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network cultivates a trust garden where each node burns cryptographic stake scaled superlinearly, C(n) = k * n^(1+epsilon), per identity. When an attacker attempts identity multiplication, marginal costs spike sharply past an unsustainable economic ledge, driving their expected net yield to an absolute nadir. This polynomial stake burning imposes deterministic friction that makes coordinated identity spoofing mathematically unviable.
